scoring.jobMethod: All-task importance-weighted beta, then percentile (share at or below), rounded to a whole number.
scoring.pathMethod: Equal mean of distinct supported jobs’ rounded, displayed percentiles; no candidates, no re-ranking. Broader group proxies use the distinct SSC members and are labelled as estimates.
scoring.missingMethod: Exclude missing scores from the mean and disclose partial coverage; never replace missing scores with zero.
scoring.colours: Checker bands: under 40 green, 40–69 amber, 70 and above red.

exampleCareer.title: Transportation engineers
exampleCareer.description: Transportation engineers design and set the engineering specifications for the construction and development of roadways and transport infrastructure. They apply engineering concepts and knowledge for developing sustainable and efficient modes of transportation ranging from roads to tunnels, bridges and railways.

tasks.text: Study traffic patterns to identify engineering problems and assess project impact.
Design plans for new transport systems including airports and motorways.
Design new or improved junctions for transport infrastructure.
Assess transport systems to determine need for modification or expansion.
Evaluate projects' impact on traffic and traffic control adequacy at development sites.

exampleCareer.title: Water engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional water engineers research and develop methods for the provision of clean water, water treatment and flood damage prevention and reaction. They design sewage systems and networks for the removal and treatment of wastewater from cities and other residential areas. They also design and construct drainage systems for sewers and storm water systems. See also 8134/99 - Water and sewerage plant operatives n.e.c.

tasks.text: Perform hydrologic, hydraulic, or water quality modelling.
Devise flood defence strategies including river and flood plain modelling.
Design pumping systems and stations for wastewater collection.
Develop water treatment programmes for different water systems.
Direct the engineering of water control, treatment, or distribution projects.

exampleCareer.title: Automotive engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional automotive engineers design and oversee the manufacturing process and operation of motor vehicles such as motorcycles, cars, trucks, buses and their respective engineering systems. They design new vehicles or mechanical parts, supervise modifications and resolve technical problems. They make sure that designs comply with cost specifications and other constraints. They also conduct research studying environmental, energy and safety aspects. See also 5231/98 - Vehicle technicians, mechanics and electricians n.e.c.

tasks.text: Solve engineering problems related to vehicle design.
Apply mechanical principles to solve specific engineering problems.
Assess new ideas for cost-effectiveness and safety.
Consider evolving customer needs and emissions regulations in new design and manufacturing processes.
Ensure drawings or models comply with engineering specifications, codes, and standards.

exampleCareer.title: Marine engineers and naval architects
exampleCareer.description: Marine engineers and naval architects, build, maintain and repair all types of boats from pleasure crafts to naval vessels, including submarines. They may design, build, maintain and repair the hull, mechanical, electronic equipment and auxiliary systems such as engines, pumps, heating, ventilation and generator sets. They analyse floating structures and take various features into account for their designs such as the form, structure, stability, resistance, access and forward force of hulls.

tasks.text: Carry out stability analyses of ships to ensure seaworthiness.
Ensure marine designs are safe, seaworthy, and cost-effective.
Develop sectional and waterline curves of hull to establish centre of gravity, ideal hull form, and buoyancy and stability data.
Establish basic characteristics of craft, such as size, weight, speed, propulsion, displacement, and draught, by studying design proposals and specifications.
Design marine apparatus and equipment.

exampleCareer.title: Mechanical design engineers
exampleCareer.description: Mechanical design engineers perform engineering duties in planning and designing tools, engines, machines, and other mechanically functioning equipment. They oversee installation, operation, maintenance, and repair of equipment such as centralised heat, gas, water, and steam systems.

tasks.text: Design and evaluate mechanical products to meet specific requirements.
Use specialist computer-aided design (CAD) software and other resources to design the systems required for the project.
Prepare designs for machines, components, or systems related to the use of mechanical or fluid energy.
Develop specifications for mechanical equipment, dies, tools, and controls using CAD equipment.
Outline mechanical designs.

exampleCareer.title: Other mechanical engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional other mechanical engineers apply engineering principles to design, develop, operate and maintain mechanical systems across sectors such as energy, transport and manufacturing. They may conduct research, provide technical advice, and oversee projects involving stress analysis, machinery design, inspection and systems integration. Roles often include ensuring compliance with standards and contributing to innovation in mechanical engineering applications This group excludes occupations categorised under sub-unit groups: 2122/01 - Automotive engineers (professional); 2122/02 - Marine engineers and naval architects and 2122/03 - Mechanical design engineers. See also 5223/14 - Mechanical engineers (technicians).

tasks.text: Apply mechanical principles to solve specific engineering problems.
Design and evaluate mechanical products to meet specific requirements.
Prepare designs for machines, components, or systems related to the use of mechanical or fluid energy.
Develop new mechanical products to enhance engineering solutions.
Test and evaluate theoretical designs to improve mechanical system performance.

exampleCareer.title: Power systems engineers
exampleCareer.description: Power systems engineers supervise the energy conversion and distribution processes. They analyse the energy supply and consumption efficiency and develop new ways to improve the existing processes. They study the environmental impact of energy use and combine the production of renewable energy in power systems.

tasks.text: Analyse energy requirements and distribution systems to maximise the use of renewable energy sources like wind or nuclear.
Integrate electrical systems with renewable energy systems for efficiency improvement.
Analyse energy data using engineering software to identify trends.
Undertake design engineering to produce detailed plans and proposals for the electricity network.
Plan the layout of electric power generating plants, distribution lines, or substations.

exampleCareer.title: Railway signalling engineers
exampleCareer.description: Railway signalling engineers design, install, and maintain signalling systems that control train movements. They ensure safe and efficient operation by developing layouts, programming interlocking systems, and conducting inspections and fault diagnosis in compliance with railway standards.

tasks.text: Comply with industry-specific safety regulations to ensure operational safety.
Ensure safe systems of work are applied, hazards and risks are identified and mitigated in their own work.
Adhere to health and safety requirements in the workplace.
Adhere to established safe working practices.
Develop integrated designs that maintain or improve the safety and reliability of the railway.

exampleCareer.title: Other electrical engineers
exampleCareer.description: Other electrical engineers  design, develop, test and maintain electrical systems and equipment across sectors such as energy, manufacturing and telecommunications. They may oversee installations, conduct diagnostics, ensure compliance with technical standards and safety, and work on specialist applications like lighting, laser systems and traction technologies. This group excludes occupations categorised under sub-unit groups: 2123/02 - Power systems engineers and 2123/03 - Railway signalling engineers.

tasks.text: Design electrical instruments and systems for various purposes.
Inspect and test electrical or electronic systems to diagnose malfunctions using oscilloscopes and voltmeters.
Inspect electrical systems, equipment, or components to identify hazards, defects, or the need for adjustment or repair, and to ensure compliance with codes.
Design engineering schematics for electrical systems using CAD software.
Set up and operate specialised or standard test equipment to diagnose, test, or analyse the performance of electronic components, assemblies, or systems.

exampleCareer.title: Broadcast engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional broadcast engineers work with hardware and broadcast systems that are used across television, radio and new media to make sure that programmes are broadcast on time and to quality specifications. As well as operating and maintaining the systems, they carry out updates and repairs. See also 5249/01 - Broadcast and communications technicians.

tasks.text: Maintain and repair broadcast equipment to ensure proper working condition.
Repair faults in broadcast equipment to maintain transmission quality.
Maintain specialist equipment for video production, broadcast, satellite transmission, and interactive media.
Quickly identify and implement alternatives to minimise service loss when equipment fails.
Inspect machinery or equipment to diagnose faults.

exampleCareer.title: Telecommunications engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional telecommunications engineers design, build, test and maintain telecommunication systems and networks, including radio and broadcasting equipment. They analyse customer needs and requirements, ensure that the equipment meets regulations, and prepare and present reports and proposals on telecommunication-related problems. Telecommunications engineers design and oversee the service delivery in all its phases, supervising the installation and use of telecommunications equipment and facilities, preparing documentation and providing training for company staff once new equipment has been installed. See also 5242/00 - Telecoms and related network installers and repairers.

tasks.text: Design telecommunications equipment to improve network performance.
Analyse electronics system requirements, capacity, cost, and customer needs to assess project feasibility.
Design, build, and test digital networks based on specific design requirements.
Find and diagnose faults in telecom networks to maintain connectivity.
Monitor network performance and troubleshoot problems and outages.

exampleCareer.title: Other electronics engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional other electronics engineers design, develop, test and integrate electronic circuits, devices and systems for applications such as defence, avionics, radar and specialist instrumentation. They may undertake research, prototyping, inspections and compliance checks, and advise on technical standards and safety. This group excludes occupations categorised under sub-unit groups: 2124/01 - Broadcast engineers (professional) and 2124/02 - Telecommunications engineers (professional). See also 5249/04 - Electronics engineers (technicians).

tasks.text: Design electronic products for various applications.
Systematically improve the detailed design of a piece of electronic equipment.
Set up and operate specialised or standard test equipment to diagnose, test, or analyse the performance of electronic components, assemblies, or systems.
Select and evaluate electronics equipment, components, or systems based on specific functional specifications.
Conduct research to test the design and performance of equipment and systems.

exampleCareer.title: Chemical engineers
exampleCareer.description: Chemical engineers design and develop large-scale chemical and physical production processes and are involved in the entire industrial process required for transforming raw materials into products.

tasks.text: Design a scalable production process transitioning from lab tests through pilot production to large-scale manufacturing.
Scale up experimental processes for large-scale industrial production.
Use computer models to work out safe and cost-effective production methods.
Determine most effective arrangement of operations such as mixing, crushing, heat transfer, distillation, and drying.
Design plant and equipment configuration so that they can be readily adapted to suit the product range and the process technologies involved, taking environmental and economic aspects into account.

exampleCareer.title: Control and instrumentation engineers
exampleCareer.description: Control and Instrumentation engineers design and develop equipment used in manufacturing processes for controlling and monitoring various engineering processes. They design equipment for the monitoring of production sites such as manufacturing systems, machinery uses and production processes.

tasks.text: Design and develop plant control systems and install them.
Test and validate automation & control systems to ensure that they are safe, functional and satisfy the requirements of a system specification, complying with national and/or international standards.
Develop or modify automation and control system programmes using a variety of different programming tools, languages and techniques.
Control and monitor a process or plant and equipment efficiently and securely, resolving problems and abnormal conditions.
Program industrial control equipment and software.

exampleCareer.title: Industrial and production engineers
exampleCareer.description: Industrial and production engineers design production systems and present solutions. They consider variables such as resource allocation, technology, ergonomics, production flows, and product specifications for the design and implementation of production systems.

tasks.text: Design new systems and processes to optimise manufacturing efficiency.
Design layout of equipment or workspaces to achieve maximum efficiency.
Establish standard production rate or improve efficiency by studying time, motion, methods, and speed involved in maintenance, production, or other operations.
Draw up production plans to optimise manufacturing processes and resource allocation.
Plan new products and production processes to optimise manufacturing operations.

exampleCareer.title: Aeronautical engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional aeronautical engineers design, develop, manufacture, maintain and modify military and civil aircraft, aeronautical components and associated systems. They use their technical knowledge to improve flight safety and fuel efficiency, reduce costs and address the environmental impact of air travel. They may also work with aircraft that operates in space such as robots and satellites. See also 5234/00 - Aircraft maintenance and related trades.

tasks.text: Design or redesign aerospace products, systems and services to fulfil defined project requirements.
Apply the principles of science and technology to create aircraft, components and support equipment.
Ensure aircraft comply with flight safety regulations.
Test and evaluate theoretical designs to ensure compliance with aviation standards.
Develop innovative solutions to complex technical engineering problems using analytical techniques.

exampleCareer.title: Aircraft engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional aircraft engineers apply scientific and technological principles to research, development and design of aircraft and their components. Aircraft engineers research design specifications for aircraft and the relevant support equipment. They may test, assemble, and modify aircraft parts. See also 5234/00 - Aircraft maintenance and related trades.

tasks.text: Apply the principles of science and technology to create aircraft, components and support equipment.
Design or redesign aerospace products, systems and services to fulfil defined project requirements.
Ensure aircraft comply with flight safety regulations.
Test and evaluate theoretical designs to ensure compliance with aviation standards.
Conduct tests on aircraft components to ensure performance and safety.

exampleCareer.title: Avionics engineers
exampleCareer.description: Avionics Engineers work in the aerospace industry designing and developing aircraft, spacecraft, satellites, missiles, and spacecraft avionics (aviation electronics) instrumentation such as the navigation, weather radar, and radio communication equipment used by pilots. They research problems associated with flight safety systems, landing gear, electronic navigation systems and test prototypes to make sure that they function according to design.

tasks.text: Systematically improve the detailed design of a piece of electronic equipment.
Test and evaluate theoretical designs to ensure compliance with aviation standards.
Design electrical instruments and systems for various purposes.
Locate and diagnose faults in aerospace equipment to ensure functionality.
Detect and diagnose faults in aircraft systems to ensure safety and compliance.

reports.title: Engineering project managers and project engineers

exampleCareer.title: Engineering project managers and project engineers
exampleCareer.description: Engineering project managers and project engineers schedule, manage and oversee engineering projects for quality of work, timeliness and completion within budget, plan, design and specify materials and equipment for the project and create necessary technical drawings.

tasks.text: Plan and coordinate a project from start to finish, including organising the schedule of work, costings and budget.
Manage projects using engineering principles and techniques.
Use project management principles and tools to scope, plan, monitor, and report on projects, ensuring required resources are allocated.
Project-manage assignments by coordinating scope, schedule, budget and deliverables.
Manage and evaluate projects to ensure they meet objectives within budget and timeline.

exampleCareer.title: Acoustic engineers
exampleCareer.description: Acoustic engineers study and apply the science of sound to various applications. They work in a wide range of areas including the elements affecting the transmission of sound in spaces for performances or recording activities, and work with construction design teams to help design buildings in order to control sound diffraction, refraction, absorption and reverberation. They also consult on the levels of noise contamination for activities that require compliance with regulations.

tasks.text: Conduct noise and vibration assessments in buildings to comply with regulations.
Operate acoustic modelling software like ODEON and SoundPLAN to simulate sound environments.
Test how changes to a building's design affect sound levels and quality.
Produce reports of findings and recommendations to enhance acoustic design and performance.
Liaise with architects, engineers and designers to understand their design requirements and provide technical advice to manufacturing and construction technicians.

exampleCareer.title: Biomedical engineers
exampleCareer.description: Biomedical engineers combine knowledge of engineering principles and biological findings for the development of medical treatments, medicaments, and general healthcare purposes. They can develop solutions ranging from the improvement of the components in conventional medicaments, implant developments, and tissue treatment.

tasks.text: Assist with designing, developing and manufacturing new medical devices to meet project requirements.
Test and refine biomedical product designs to ensure safety and efficacy.
Use computer software and mathematical models to design and develop new materials, devices, and equipment.
Test new devices and systems to diagnose and treat health conditions.
Address quality control issues to ensure the safety and efficacy of biomedical products.

exampleCareer.title: Brewers (qualified)
exampleCareer.description: Qualified brewers oversee the process of brewing beer or cider. They take responsibility for raw materials, operatives and technicians, as well as maintaining the safe and effective running of the plant and machinery. See also 8111/01 - Brewery and distillery workers.

tasks.text: Monitor fermentation processes and check temperatures.
Oversee the quality of finished products against recipe specifications.
Make quality checks at each production stage.
Carry out tests and monitor performance of processes throughout stages of production to determine degree of control over variables such as temperature, density, specific gravity, and pressure.
Monitor production for consistency.

exampleCareer.title: Clinical Engineers
exampleCareer.description: Clinical engineers apply engineering principles and materials technology to healthcare equipment. They research, design and develop medical products, such as joint replacements or robotic surgical instruments. They design or modify equipment for clients with special needs in a rehabilitation setting or manage the use of clinical equipment in hospitals and the community.

tasks.text: Examine medical equipment to protect patients and staff from electrical or mechanical hazards.
Check the safety of equipment and devices.
Carry out mechanical safety checks for healthcare engineering specialist equipment.
Check equipment to ensure that it is operating and functioning correctly.
Diagnose and address equipment faults to ensure operational efficiency.

exampleCareer.title: Energy engineers
exampleCareer.description: Energy engineers design, develop, or evaluate energy-related projects or programs to reduce energy costs and improve energy efficiency during the designing, building, or remodelling stages of construction of power generation plants.

tasks.text: Conduct energy audits to evaluate energy use and to identify conservation and cost reduction measures.
Calculate potential energy savings for specific systems or projects.
Develop strategies to reduce energy consumption.
Evaluate the technical feasibility of energy-saving measures based on engineering and energy use knowledge.
Analyse metered data to track energy consumption and identify trends.

exampleCareer.title: Food technologists
exampleCareer.description: Food technologists develop processes for manufacturing foodstuffs and related products based on chemical, physical, and biological principles as well as technology. They design and plan layouts or equipment, oversee staff, engage in controlling and improving food technologies in food production processes.

tasks.text: Develop new food products to meet consumer demands.
Modify existing products and processes to enhance food quality and safety.
Design the processes and machinery for making products with a consistent flavour, colour and texture in large quantities.
Test new products for flavour, texture, colour, nutritional content, and compliance with standards.
Ensure production processes comply with hygiene regulations.

exampleCareer.title: Gas engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional gas engineers develop methods to optimise the extraction and production of gas for energy and utilities. They design systems for gas production, supervise production operations and develop improvements on existing systems. See also 5315/00 - Plumbers & heating and ventilation installers and repairers.

tasks.text: Analyse and interpret geological, geochemical, or geophysical information from sources like survey data, well logs, boreholes, or aerial photos.
Develop geological models to understand subsurface structures, rock characteristics, and resource distribution.
Compile detailed development plans of reservoir performance using mathematical models.
Evaluate and recommend enhancements for gas flow rates.
Troubleshoot problems with gas collection systems.

exampleCareer.title: Heating and ventilating engineers (professional)
exampleCareer.description: Professional heating and ventilation (HVAC) engineers design and develop heating, ventilation, and air conditioning for use in residences, manufacturing sites, offices, or commercial buildings among others. They develop solutions that serve the needs of clients. See also 5315/00 - Plumbers & heating and ventilation installers and repairers.

tasks.text: Deliver appropriate and effective technical building services engineering solutions, by selecting, reviewing and evaluating data and technical information, and by using a range of appropriate engineering methods and processes, including the undertaking of complex calculations.
Design the arrangement of pipework, ducts, and control panels for building systems.
Carry out calculations and analyse outputs for building services engineering.
Design integrated mechanical or alternative systems to improve energy efficiency.
Use Computer Aided Design (CAD) to support building service engineering solutions.

exampleCareer.title: Materials engineers
exampleCareer.description: Materials engineers research and study the structures and chemical properties of various natural and synthetic or composite materials, including metals, alloys, rubber, ceramics, semiconductors, polymers, and glass. They determine ways to strengthen or combine materials or develop new materials with new or specific properties for use in a variety of products and applications.

tasks.text: Determine ways to strengthen or combine materials for use in various products.
Carry out specific tests on materials to assess their properties.
Make recommendations for material selection based on strength, weight, heat resistance, electrical conductivity, and cost.
Develop new materials for improved product performance.
Select the best combination of materials for specific purposes.

exampleCareer.title: Mechatronic engineers
exampleCareer.description: Mechatronics engineers design and develop intelligent systems through combining technologies from robotics, electronics, computer science, telecommunications, systems, control, and product engineering.

tasks.text: Consider the interface between mechanical and electrical elements during product design.
Design advanced electronic control systems for mechanical systems.
Model and analyse electrical circuits and mechanical systems for performance prediction.
Develop control circuits or algorithms for electromechanical or pneumatic devices.
Develop or modify automation and control system programmes using a variety of different programming tools, languages and techniques.

exampleCareer.title: Nuclear engineers
exampleCareer.description: Nuclear engineers plan and design engineering equipment and processes in nuclear plants and sites. They engage in engineering activities pertaining to nuclear power plants and develop risk solutions.

tasks.text: Design nuclear reactor cores and radiation shielding.
Design nuclear reactors and power stations.
Design new nuclear plants.
Understand the science behind how nuclear facilities work.
Modify nuclear equipment used in operations to ensure safety and compliance with regulatory standards.

exampleCareer.title: Patent engineers
exampleCareer.description: Patent engineers are patent professional who is typically involved in preparing and prosecuting patent applications. They are usually patent professionals with scientific or engineering backgrounds that do not require either attorney or patent agent qualifications, but still work with patent applications. The position involves many of the technical aspects of patent prosecution, including giving technical expertise during invention evaluation.

tasks.text: Write detailed technical descriptions of inventions in precise legal terms (patent drafts) to meet the correct legal standards.
Search through earlier publications, technical literature, and online databases to ensure the patent application is new.
Analyse scientific documents and patents to assess an invention's novelty and innovation.
Investigate each application to ascertain that the invention is described clearly and in such a way that a skilled person would be able to use it.
Assess inventions for technical feasibility and innovation.

exampleCareer.title: Robotics engineers
exampleCareer.description: Robotics engineers design and develop robotic devices and applications in conjunction with mechanical engineering principles. They also use pre-established designs for improving or inventing systems, machinery and equipment. They combine several knowledge fields such as computing, engineering, and electronics in the development of new engineering applications.

tasks.text: Build, integrate and test functional robot systems.
Program robots to perform tasks in various working environments.
Write algorithms or programming code for ad hoc robotic applications.
Test prototypes and analyse results.
Develop innovative solutions to complex technical engineering problems using analytical techniques.

exampleCareer.title: Traffic engineers
exampleCareer.description: Traffic engineers study and analyse the habits of road and motorway users and improve transportation networks with the information they gather, to achieve the best traffic conditions.

tasks.text: Study traffic patterns to identify engineering problems and assess project impact.
Recommend methods to improve traffic flow and safety.
Study accident 'black spots' to design road safety improvements.
Analyse and interpret data from transport studies.
Analyse information from traffic counting programmes.

jobs.title: Programme managers and directors (excludes IT and educational establishments)

exampleCareer.title: IT project managers
exampleCareer.description: IT project managers manage, coordinate and technically supervise specific IT projects of a discrete duration and/or budget.

tasks.text: Project-manage assignments by coordinating scope, schedule, budget and deliverables.
Manage and evaluate projects to ensure they meet objectives within budget and timeline.
Use project management principles and tools to scope, plan, monitor, and report on projects, ensuring required resources are allocated.
Plan and coordinate a project from start to finish, including organising the schedule of work, costings and budget.
Project manage activities to ensure timely delivery and meet stakeholder and budget requirements.

jobs.title: Cyber security management and governance specialists

exampleCareer.title: IT information managers
exampleCareer.description: IT information managers ensure that information is managed correctly. They classify, structure, store, disseminate and protect information.

tasks.text: Manage information and records.
Manage databases and records to keep organisational information accurate and accessible.
Ensure the security, including cyber security of all information disseminated and stored.
Validate and manage information in both digital and hard copy formats.
Establish and implement systems for the management, sharing and storage of project information according to required protocols throughout the lifecycle of the project.

exampleCareer.title: IT product managers
exampleCareer.description: IT product managers analyse and define current and target status for IT products, services or solutions. They estimate the cost effectiveness, points of risk, opportunities, strengths and weaknesses of products or services provided. Product managers create structured plans and establish time scales and milestones, ensuring optimisation of activities and resources.

tasks.text: Develop a compelling product vision and strategy with teams and stakeholders.
Develop an expert understanding of users' needs and champion these in product delivery.
Develop and prioritise the product backlog, create user stories, and make evidence-based decisions.
Oversee all aspects of product development and marketing to ensure its success.
Create timelines and roadmaps for product development.

exampleCareer.title: IT service delivery managers
exampleCareer.description: IT service delivery managers oversee a number of key functions within the IT department that enable the delivery of a high quality service. This can include applications, data storage and other business resources. IT service delivery managers cover the design, development, deployment, operation and withdrawal of services to users.

tasks.text: Manage and maintain quality levels in service delivery.
Supervise the delivery of a quality service that supports the department in achieving overall business objectives.
Develop and implement IT service improvement plans to meet colleagues' requirements with minimal disruption.
Address IT issues by prioritising in response to customer service level agreements.
Respond to technology service incidents using agreed service management practices.

exampleCareer.title: IT systems managers
exampleCareer.description: IT systems managers plan, direct or coordinate activities in fields such as electronic data processing, information systems, systems analysis and computer programming.

tasks.text: Manage daily operations of the department, including workflow analysis and priority setting.
Analyse information processing needs to plan computer systems.
Direct the work of systems and business analysts, developers, and support specialists.
Establish requirements for new systems or modifications in consultation with staff, users, and management.
Implement strategic computing initiatives.

exampleCareer.title: IT test managers
exampleCareer.description: IT test managers work on testing apps, programs, software production and the Internet of Things (IoT) for end users. They test software for usability and functionality.

tasks.text: Conduct testing on various software applications to detect defects and ensure they are fit for purpose.
Design testing scenarios to simulate real-world use.
Design test plans to outline testing procedures.
Conduct different software test types including functional, non-functional, and structural testing.
Carry out manual and automated software tests to meet project deadlines.

exampleCareer.title: Network managers
exampleCareer.description: Network managers supervise the design, installation and running of IT, data and telephony systems in an organisation.

tasks.text: Supervise engineers or other staff in the design or implementation of network solutions.
Monitor network performance and troubleshoot problems and outages.
Monitor networks to ensure availability to system users.
Oversee implementation of network security measures to protect data integrity.
Design and maintain secure network infrastructure solutions.

exampleCareer.title: Software development managers
exampleCareer.description: Software development managers oversee the development of software systems to provide support to all organisational units. They monitor the results and quality of the different software solutions and projects implemented in the organisation.

tasks.text: Recruit, employ, train, and supervise staff to deliver software projects.
Direct the work of systems and business analysts, developers, and support specialists.
Supervise programmers in their development tasks.
Manage daily operations of the department, including workflow analysis and priority setting.
Establish requirements for new systems or modifications in consultation with staff, users, and management.

exampleCareer.title: Technical support managers
exampleCareer.description: Technical support managers monitor the delivery of technical support services to clients according to the predefined deadlines. They plan and organise the user support actions and troubleshoot IT problems and issues.

tasks.text: Recruit, employ, train, and supervise staff to provide technical support services.
Monitor, record and respond to requests for support.
Solve IT-related user problems.
Manage daily operations of the department, including workflow analysis and priority setting.
Troubleshoot hardware, software, or network problems.

exampleCareer.title: IT infrastructure managers
exampleCareer.description: IT infrastructure managers are responsible for planning, leading, and coordinating the delivery and operation of an organisation's IT infrastructure. This includes data centres, servers, storage, networks, cloud platforms, and core services. They set standards and policies to ensure capacity, performance, availability, security, and resilience are maintained across systems. Their role involves managing incident response, change control, and problem resolution processes, while also overseeing supplier relationships and asset management. They lead teams that handle infrastructure builds, migrations, maintenance, and decommissioning. In addition, they manage budgets, monitor service levels, and provide technical governance to support infrastructure roadmaps and lifecycle planning.

tasks.text: Devise plans to implement and improve IT infrastructure and application change projects, identifying organisational needs.
Recruit, employ, train, and supervise staff to maintain IT operations.
Oversee IT security operations.
Carry out administrative or managerial functions, such as taking responsibility for a team's staff, budget, planning, or long-term objectives.
Develop and implement IT service improvement plans to meet colleagues' requirements with minimal disruption.

exampleCareer.title: Computer analysts and scientists
exampleCareer.description: Computer analysts and scientists conduct research in computer and information science. They invent and design new approaches to computing technology, find innovative uses for existing technology, and solve complex problems in computing.

tasks.text: Research and develop new technologies.
Develop new technology by applying theoretical expertise and innovation in computer applications.
Develop computational methods to solve problems in science, engineering, business, or industry.
Use computer simulations and mathematical modelling in research and development work.
Design software systems using scientific analysis and mathematical models.

exampleCareer.title: Data architects
exampleCareer.description: Data architects design and build data models to fulfil the strategic data needs of the business. They design the upgrade, management, de-commission and archive of data in compliance with data policy and design as well as manage data dictionaries.

tasks.text: Develop data models.
Develop database architectural strategies at modelling, design, and implementation stages for business requirements.
Identify organisational information requirements and model data solutions using conceptual data modelling techniques.
Map out the conceptual design for a planned database.
Refine the logical design so that it can be translated into a specific data model.

exampleCareer.title: Data engineers
exampleCareer.description: Data engineers develop and construct data products and services. They integrate them into systems and business processes. They identify opportunities to re-use existing data flows, build data-streaming systems, and manage databases.

tasks.text: Set up and maintain automated data processes.
Develop and architect robust data sourcing and processing systems for the organisation.
Structure, clean, and manipulate data, and design and oversee its collection and transformation.
Develop data warehouse process models, including sourcing, loading, transformation, and extraction.
Develop and implement methods and systems for acquiring, compiling, synthesising, extracting and reporting information.

exampleCareer.title: IT systems architects
exampleCareer.description: IT system architects design architecture, components, modules, interfaces, and data for a multi-components systems to meet specified requirements.

tasks.text: Develop proposed solution designs, including system architecture.
Design the architecture of the components of an application.
Analyse business and technical requirements to select and specify appropriate technology solutions.
Verify stability, interoperability, portability, security, and scalability of system architecture.
Participate in architectural planning and design.

exampleCareer.title: IT business analysts
exampleCareer.description: IT business analysts are in charge of analysing and designing an organisation's processes and systems, assessing the business model and its integration with technology. They identify change needs, assess the impact of the change, capture and document requirements and then ensure that these requirements are delivered whilst supporting the business through the implementation process.

tasks.text: Analyse business problems with stakeholders to clarify requirements.
Collect detailed requirements from clients and users for IT projects.
Distinguish, analyse and document business requirements and manage those requirements throughout a project life cycle.
Analyse business models to identify IT system requirements.
Analyse business processes to identify opportunities for improvement.

exampleCareer.title: IT solutions architects and designers
exampleCareer.description: IT solution architects and designers lead teams that design, develop and demonstrate new computer systems for clients.

tasks.text: Develop proposed solution designs, including system architecture.
Design the architecture of the components of an application.
Analyse business and technical requirements to select and specify appropriate technology solutions.
Develop detailed designs for new systems and products.
Make architectural judgements and solve design problems.

exampleCareer.title: Computer games designers
exampleCareer.description: Computer games designers design core features of video games. They specify in innovative game and role-play mechanics, story lines, and character biographies. They also create and maintain design documentation. Additionally, they guide and collaborate with production staff to produce games as designed.

tasks.text: Plan and detail the setting, rules, and story flow of a new game.
Create original ideas for projects to develop innovative gaming experiences.
Transform a rough idea into a detailed concept.
Design role-play mechanics for new video games.
Develop design level documentation, including mechanics and guidelines, for projects.

exampleCareer.title: Computer programmers
exampleCareer.description: Computer programmers are responsible for writing testing, debugging/troubleshooting and maintaining the source code of computer programs.

tasks.text: Write programmes by breaking down specifications into simplest elements and translating them into a programming language.
Write logical and maintainable software solutions in line with given specifications to meet the design requirements and organisational coding standards.
Write new programmes to meet customer requirements using current programming languages.
Evaluate and debug software code to ensure functionality.
Test programmes for errors to ensure software reliability.

exampleCareer.title: Software developers
exampleCareer.description: Software developers design, program, build, deploy and maintain software using many different skills and tools. They also help build software systems that power networks and devices and ensure that those systems remain functional.

tasks.text: Design and develop software systems to meet specific user requirements.

exampleCareer.description: Art therapists help patients overcome psychological and emotional difficulties and facilitate self-understanding through an artistic process which reflects emotions and feelings.

exampleCareer.description: Chiropractors and osteopaths use their hands to help relieve problems with the musculoskeletal system. exampleCareer.description: Music therapists use music creatively to help their clients address social, emotional or physical difficulties.

exampleCareer.description: Nutritionists use food science knowledge to help individuals and groups make the right choices about what they eat. exampleCareer.description: Psychological wellbeing practitioners assess and support adults who are experiencing common mental health difficulties such as mild to moderate symptoms of depression, anxiety and low mood.

exampleCareer.description: Infection prevention and control nurses (IPC) work to stop the spread of infections in healthcare and community settings by creating and implementing policies, educating staff and the public, and monitoring for outbreaks. tasks.text: Catalogue books, publications, films, audio-visual aids, and other library materials.
Catalogue acquired information for library systems.
Develop and manage collections of books, journals, and websites.
Classify, collate, and catalogue information using special computer applications.
Provide reader, advisory and information services to the public and local businesses.

exampleCareer.title: Archivists
exampleCareer.description: Archivists preserve information and make it accessible to users, increasingly in digital format. Archives may include valuable historical books, papers, maps and plans, as well as photographs, prints, films, tapes, videos and computer-generated records.

tasks.text: Maintain archives to ensure the safekeeping of historical documents.
Safely and securely store and preserve information and collections.
Organise archival records to facilitate access.
Manage storage conditions for records and archives, ensuring compliance with standards and risk management.
Assess records for preservation and retention.

exampleCareer.title: Collection managers and curators
exampleCareer.description: Collection managers and curators are responsible for exhibits in a museum or art gallery. They build up collections, often in specialist areas, and develop ways in which objects, archives and artworks can be interpreted, through exhibitions, publications, events and audio-visual presentations.

tasks.text: Display objects or collections in a way that makes them accessible and engaging to the general public.
Plan and organise exhibitions and shows.
Acquire objects or collections of interest to the museum or gallery.
Display artefacts in museum exhibitions.
Select, purchase or borrow items for exhibitions or collections.

exampleCareer.title: Conservators
exampleCareer.description: Conservators preserve and restore works of art, buildings, books and furniture of historical importance by applying restoration techniques. They ensure that conditions are right for display and storage.

tasks.text: Conserve and preserve manuscripts, records, and other artefacts.
Perform conservation tasks using instruments like scalpels, cotton buds, and solvents to restore artefacts.
Apply treatments to reduce decay in historical artefacts and preserve them.
Follow conservation ethics and procedures in restoration activities.
Assess fragile items for careful handling, repair, or conservation.

exampleCareer.title: Museum education officers
exampleCareer.description: Museum education officers develop learning opportunities in museums, galleries, stately homes or in a community-based role. Learning events are aimed at classes, groups or individuals and can be formal or informal.

tasks.text: Design and implement engaging learning activities to inspire and educate participants.
Research and develop educational programmes and resources for schools, adults, families, community groups or visitors to sites of special environmental interest.
Develop programmes of talks, activities and workshops around particular exhibitions or in response to particular themes or annual festivals.
Liaise with schools, colleges and teachers to promote the use of the museum's collections and activities in line with the national curriculum.
Work with teachers to deliver educational content.

exampleCareer.title: Garment technologists
exampleCareer.description: Garment technologists oversee every stage of garment production, from sourcing the correct fabrics, to design then manufacture. They are involved in choosing the correct fabric ensuring it is fit for purpose, and making sure production remains within budget. They work closely alongside designers, pattern cutters and buyers.

tasks.text: Review and assess garments for fit, quality, cost, and finish against design specifications and customer requirements.
Source fabrics and textiles that are suitable for the product they are intended for.
Determine appropriate materials and production techniques based on product specifications.
Understand design from a technical perspective, such as producing patterns and technical specifications for designs.
Inspect garments for quality compliance.

jobs.title: Engineering project managers and project engineers

exampleCareer.title: Planning engineers
exampleCareer.description: Planning engineers decide and develop the most appropriate economic models and engineering methods for projects. They work in a variety of fields such as civil engineering or construction. Planning engineers are normally onsite during an engineering project to supervise all stages of work and provide solutions.

tasks.text: Plan and coordinate a project from start to finish, including organising the schedule of work, costings and budget.
Create project timetables to ensure timely completion.
Utilise specialist software to develop and manage planning programmes.
Assess construction methods and determine cost-effectiveness of plans, using computer models.
Manage projects using engineering principles and techniques.

exampleCareer.title: Quality control engineers
exampleCareer.description: Quality control engineers define quality standards for the creation of products or services. They check to make sure the products and services are in compliance with the quality standards, and they coordinate quality improvements.

tasks.text: Devise and establish a company's quality procedures, standards and specifications.
Set quality standards for manufacturing processes to ensure product excellence.
Develop quality control/assurance plans for responsible products, services, or projects, focusing on aspects like dimensional control and timely delivery.
Monitor product quality to ensure compliance with standards and specifications.
Establish quality assurance controls and documentation procedures.

exampleCareer.title: Compliance and regulatory professionals
exampleCareer.description: Compliance and regulatory professionals ensure that organisations comply with industry specifications, standards, regulations and laws. They review operational practices, create and enforce compliance plans and perform regulatory risk management. They may be employed by organisations or work as consultants.

tasks.text: Ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.
Monitor compliance with laws, regulations and internal policies.
Ensure compliance with governing bodies' requirements, rules, and regulations.
Develop and implement compliance controls within the organisation.
Review and interpret new regulations to ensure company compliance.

exampleCareer.title: Quality assurance professionals
exampleCareer.description: Quality assurance professionals aim to ensure that the products or services an organisation provides are fit for purpose, legally compliant and meet customer expectation.

tasks.text: Devise and establish a company's quality procedures, standards and specifications.
Conduct quality assurance checks to ensure product standards are met.
Establish quality assurance controls and documentation procedures.
Develop quality control/assurance plans for responsible products, services, or projects, focusing on aspects like dimensional control and timely delivery.
Conduct quality assurance checks and rectify or report issues.

exampleCareer.title: Environmental health professionals
exampleCareer.description: Environmental health professionals use specialist technical skills and knowledge to protect people from health risks associated with the environment in which they live and work. They maintain and safeguard standards, including taking legal action to enforce relevant legislation with regard to public health policy.

tasks.text: Identify instances of non-compliance with environmental health legislation and determine the most appropriate action.
Identify hazards and assess risks to human health on environmental health matters.
Conduct environmental hazard inspections to identify or quantify problems, such as asbestos, poor air quality, water contamination, or other environmental hazards.
Enforce health legislation to promote public health and understanding of health protection procedures.
Investigate environmental hazards.

jobs.title: Newspaper and periodical journalists and reporters

exampleCareer.title: Newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors
exampleCareer.description: Newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors evaluate, manage and oversee the editorial direction for the style and content of features and stories for broadcasting and for newspapers, magazines, news websites and periodicals.

tasks.text: Exercise editorial judgement on the best angle to approach a story.
Supervise the editing process.
Develop story or content ideas considering reader or audience appeal.
Examine news items of local, national, and international significance to determine topics to address.
Supervise and coordinate work of reporters and other editors.

jobs.title: Newspaper and periodical journalists and reporters

exampleCareer.title: Broadcast journalists
exampleCareer.description: Broadcast journalists research, investigate and present news and current affairs content for television, radio and the internet.

tasks.text: Gather information on news subjects through research, interviews, and observation.
Prepare and present material on air for pre-recorded and live pieces.
Research, verify and collate evidence and information from sources like the internet, archives, and databases to support a story.

exampleCareer.description: Newspaper and periodical journalists and reporters research and write stories for national, regional and local press.

tasks.text: Gather information on news subjects through research, interviews, and observation.
Produce concise and accurate copy for newspapers according to house style and strict deadlines.
Conduct interviews to collect information for news articles.
Research, verify and collate evidence and information from sources like the internet, archives, and databases to support a story.

exampleCareer.title: Press officers
exampleCareer.description: Press officers represent their organisation to the media. They encompass both reactive and proactive functions, they deal with the national and regional print media, broadcast and online media.

tasks.text: Prepare press releases to communicate organisational news and public announcements.
Respond to media enquiries.
Coordinate media engagements with reporters, journalists, and editors.

exampleCareer.title: Public relations officers
exampleCareer.description: Public relations officers represent a company or organisation to stakeholders and the public. They use communications strategies to promote an understanding of the activities and image of their clients in a favourable way.

tasks.text: Develop public relations strategies that influence public opinion or promote ideas, products, or services by studying the objectives, promotional policies, or needs of organisations.

exampleCareer.title: Social media managers
exampleCareer.description: Social media managers manage an organisation's online presence by developing a strategy, producing good content, analysing usage data, facilitating customer service and managing projects and campaigns.

tasks.text: Manage social media for an organisation.
Develop social media strategies to engage with the audience.
Create posts for social media to engage with the audience.
Manage and update information and engage with users on social media sites such as X, Facebook and Instagram.

exampleCareer.title: Advertising account managers
exampleCareer.description: Advertising account managers work within an advertising or multi-service agency, acting as a link between the agency and its clients. tasks.text: Act as the intermediary between the client and the advertising agency, maintaining regular contact with both.
Manage client accounts to maintain and enhance customer relationships.
Attend client briefings to discuss and identify their advertising requirements.
Liaise with clients, agency staff and external suppliers of goods and services.

exampleCareer.title: Creative directors
exampleCareer.description: Creative directors manage the team that is responsible for the creation of advertisements and commercials. They oversee the whole creation process. Creative directors pitch the designs of their team to the client.

tasks.text: Oversee the creative team's ideas and projects.
Develop creative ideas and concepts in partnership with the art director.
Develop advertising concepts with staff.
Generate creative ideas based on client's requirements.
Lead projects from start to end to deliver innovative design solutions.

exampleCareer.title: Fundraising managers
exampleCareer.description: Fundraising managers are responsible for raising money on behalf of organisations, often non-profit such as charities. They manage the fundraised resources and develop programmes for its use. They perform a variety of tasks to raise money such as developing corporate partnerships, coordinating direct mail campaigns, organising fundraisers, contacting donators or sponsors and sourcing grant income from trusts, foundations and other statutory bodies.

tasks.text: Oversee fundraising activities to meet financial goals.
Raise and manage funds for organisational needs.
Identify, build and maintain relationships to raise financial and non-financial support for the charitable cause.

exampleCareer.title: Chemical laboratory technicians
exampleCareer.description: Chemical laboratory technicians support scientists to carry out chemical processes and conduct tests to analyse chemical substances for manufacturing or scientific purposes. Chemical laboratory technicians perform laboratory activities, test chemical substances, analyse data and report about their work. They observe and monitor laboratory activities, record test sequences and analyse the results.

tasks.text: Adhere to health and safety requirements in the workplace.
Carry out laboratory tasks following specified methodologies, such as Standard Operating Procedures.
Perform laboratory tests to produce reliable data for scientific investigations.

exampleCareer.title: Health physics monitors
exampleCareer.description: Health physics monitors monitor radiation levels in buildings and facilities to ensure compliance with health and safety standards and to prevent dangerous elevations in the radiation level. tasks.text: Measure and identify radiation types in work areas and equipment using radiation detectors.

exampleCareer.title: Laboratory food technicians
exampleCareer.description: Laboratory food technicians assist food technologists in the development of processes for manufacturing foodstuffs and related products based on chemical, physical and biological principles. They perform research and experiments on ingredients, additives and packaging. Food technicians also check product quality to ensure compliance with legislation and regulations. They perform standardised tests to determine the chemical, physical, or microbiological features of products for human consumption.

tasks.text: Test the safety and quality of food.
Aid in quality control processes for food products.

Perform laboratory tests to produce reliable data for scientific investigations.

exampleCareer.title: Medical laboratory technicians
exampleCareer.description: Medical laboratory technicians work under supervision of biomedical scientists to carry out laboratory procedures. They work in the pre-analytical handling of samples such as checking the details of specimens received for analysis, maintaining analysers, loading reagents and packaging specimens. They also perform clerical tasks such as monitoring the stock levels of reagents used in analysis.

tasks.text: Carry out laboratory tasks following specified methodologies, such as Standard Operating Procedures.

exampleCareer.description: Other laboratory technicians perform technical and practical tasks to support scientific, analytical, and experimental work in laboratories across various fields, for occupations that fall outside sub-unit groups: 3111/02 - Chemical laboratory technicians; 3111/03 - Health physics monitors; 3111/04 - Laboratory food technicians and 3111/05 - Medical laboratory technicians. They prepare and maintain equipment, collect and process samples, conduct routine tests and measurements, record and analyse data, and ensure compliance with health, safety, and quality standards. Work may involve assisting in research, teaching, or industrial processes.

tasks.text: Perform laboratory tests to produce reliable data for scientific investigations.
Carry out laboratory tasks following specified methodologies, such as Standard Operating Procedures.
Set up, clean, and maintain laboratory equipment.

exampleCareer.title: Aerospace technicians
exampleCareer.description: Aerospace technicians work with aerospace engineers to operate, maintain and test equipment used on aircraft. They record test procedures and results and make recommendations for changes.

exampleCareer.title: Wind turbine technicians
exampleCareer.description: Wind turbine technicians maintain and repair wind turbines by performing diagnostic inspections, analysing faults and performing repair duties. Wind turbine technicians may also test and install hardware and software components of wind turbines.

tasks.text: Identify and diagnose faults in wind turbines to maximise energy output.

exampleCareer.title: Building technicians
exampleCareer.description: Building technicians assist engineers and surveyors with essential tasks on construction projects and building works. They can oversee a range of tasks, from monitoring build progress, to negotiating with suppliers, preparing site plans and estimating costs.

exampleCareer.description: Civil engineering technicians give technical support to engineers on construction projects.
